ic_name: HDMI / DVI TMDS (TI TFP410 PanelBus Digital Transmitter — subset)
module_role: DVI 1.0 / HDMI video-only transmitter. Sits between a graphics controller's parallel RGB pixel interface (24-bit single-edge or 12-bit dual-edge with DE/HSYNC/VSYNC/CTL) and the DVI / HDMI connector. Encodes per-pixel RGB to 10-bit T.M.D.S. characters, serialises onto 3 differential data pairs + 1 differential clock pair, drives current-mode differential outputs to a DVI/HDMI receiver across a twisted-pair cable. Optional sideband I2C target/DDC bridge for register access + EDID/HDCP transport.

integration_overview.physical_topology: All devices' SDA pins connected together; all SCL pins connected together; both lines pulled up to VDD via Rp.
integration_overview.drive_type: Open-drain / open-collector wired-AND (push-pull in Ultra Fast-mode only).
integration_overview.voltage_domain: VDD-dependent; mixed-voltage operation supported via Rp to highest VDD on bus (or via voltage-level translator).
integration_overview.max_devices: Limited by total bus capacitance Cb (typ ≤ 400 pF for Sm/Fm; ≤ 550 pF for Fm+) and address-space (≈ 112 free 7-bit addresses).
integration_overview.no_chip_select: TMDS is point-to-point; no CS on the TMDS wires.
integration_overview.wire_count_sideband: 5 typical (SCL + SDA for DDC/I2C + HPD/HTPLG + RSEN via MSEN + reset/ISEL)
integration_overview.wire_directions: TMDS data + clock pairs: source → sink (unidirectional). Sideband I2C: bidirectional. HPD: sink → source. RSEN: source-side passive sense.
integration_overview.no_addressing_on_TMDS: No device address on TMDS; one transmitter ↔ one receiver per link.
integration_overview.addressing_on_I2C: TFP410 self register file at base 0b0111_A3A2A1 (A[3:1] pin-strap); DDC EDID at 0x50; HDCP at 0x3A (cipher outside TFP410 scope).
integration_overview.controller_choices: Graphics controller is the universal pixel source; TFP410 is the TMDS PHY + encoder bridge.
integration_overview.handshake_at_protocol_layer: None on TMDS — fire-and-forget streaming. I2C uses standard ACK/NAK + arbitration.

interface_categories: Mixed (e.g. master with optional slave fallback after arbitration loss)
interconnect_topologies_supported: Single master + N slaves (each addressed by unique 7/10-bit address)
Multi-master + multi-slave (true multi-master bus with arbitration on SDA)
Hub / repeater / extender / multiplexer / bridge for expanding capacitance or reach
default_signal_values_when_idle: SDA = HIGH, SCL = HIGH (both released, pulled up by Rp). The bus is 'free' after tBUF following a STOP condition.
soc_dependent_items: Pad type (open-drain output + Schmitt input + glitch filter)
Pull-up resistor sizing (depends on VDD, Cb, target rise time)
Bus speed (selected per device capability + bus load)
Interrupt source mapping (ACK fail, arbitration loss, bus error, byte complete, START/STOP detect)
Software vs hardware addressing (some I2C controllers latch their slave address from external pins)
Glitch filter spike-suppression length (typically 50 ns for Fm)

low_power_modes.bus_idle: Both SDA and SCL HIGH; static; no power consumption beyond Rp leakage.
low_power_modes.device_sleep: Device must continue to pull SDA HIGH (release) when sleeping; on wakeup it must respond to its address within the timing budget.
low_power_modes.Power_down_PD_eq_0: Only digital I/O buffers + I2C interface remain active; TMDS drivers + PLL + encoders all gated; minimal current (I_PD ≤ 500 µA typical).
low_power_modes.TDIS_eq_1: TMDS circuitry disabled while PD=1; PLL may stay locked; faster wake-up than full PD.
low_power_modes.VEN_HEN_eq_0: VSYNC / HSYNC inputs transmitted as fixed LOW — does NOT reduce power but disables sync transmission.

bus_clear_procedure: If SDA stuck LOW: master sends 9 SCL clock pulses to allow the device holding SDA LOW to release it. If SCL stuck LOW: use HW reset pin or cycle power.
default_signal_values_when_omitted: Unused CTL inputs default LOW via weak pull-downs. NC tied HIGH. PD defaults 0 (powered down) after RESET.
typical_use_cases: DVI 1.0 set-top box / DVD / Blu-ray output (WUXGA 1920×1200 @ 60 Hz, 1080p).
Reference DVI/HDMI PHY for academic projects.
